questions.stem: Which regulations apply to employees working on Canadian-registered vessels and are made under Part II of the Canada Labour Code?
options: The Marine Personnel Regulations
The Collision Regulations
The Maritime Occupational Health and Safety Regulations
The Vessel Pollution and Dangerous Chemicals Regulations
questions.explanation: The MOHS define 'Act' as Part II of the Canada Labour Code and apply to employees employed on vessels registered in Canada. The others are made under the Canada Shipping Act, 2001 and deal with other subjects.

questions.stem: In what order must an employer address a hazard under MOHS s. 124(1)?
options: Provide personal protective equipment first, then try to eliminate the hazard later
Reduce it, post a warning sign, then remove the worker from the area
Administrative procedures, then protective equipment, then elimination
Eliminate it, reduce or isolate it, then protective equipment, then procedures
questions.explanation: Section 124(1) sets elimination first, reduction (including isolation) second, protective equipment third, administrative procedures fourth. PPE is not the first answer.

questions.stem: When must protection equipment be used under MOHS s. 138?
options: When the hazard cannot be eliminated or controlled and the equipment helps
Only in port, never at sea, where it could snag on gear
Only when a supervisor is present to watch the work
Whenever a worker is on deck, whatever the job
questions.explanation: Section 138(1) sets those two conditions. The equipment also must not in itself create a hazard.

questions.stem: A deckhand is to work on an unguarded platform 2.8 m above the nearest permanent safe level. What is required?
options: Only a hard hat and safety boots
The employer must provide a fall-protection system
A life jacket worn instead of any fall protection system
Nothing, because the threshold is 5 m
questions.explanation: Section 144(1)(a) requires fall protection for an unguarded work area more than 2.4 m above the nearest permanent safe level. 2.8 m is above that.

questions.stem: A structure covered by Part 2 of the MOHS is 2.7 m above a permanent safe level and the person is not on a ladder. Is a fall-protection system required by s. 144(1)(b)?
options: Yes; the threshold for every structure is 2.4 m
Yes; any height above 1.5 m requires it
No; fall protection is never required on a structure
No; the structure threshold is more than 3 m
questions.explanation: Section 144(1)(b) applies to a structure more than 3 m above a permanent safe level. The 2.4 m figure applies to unguarded work areas and to ladders where only one hand can be used. (Other duties, such as guardrails, may still apply to the structure.)

questions.stem: Which set gives the three fall-arrest figures in s. 144?
options: Anchor 17.8 kN, peak arrest force 8 kN, free fall 1.2 m
Anchor 17.8 kN, peak arrest force 1.2 kN, free fall 8 m
Anchor 8 kN, peak arrest force 17.8 kN, free fall 1.2 m
Anchor 2.4 kN, peak arrest force 3 kN, free fall 1.5 m
questions.explanation: The anchor must withstand 17.8 kN, a fall-arrest system must limit peak arrest force to 8 kN, and it must prevent free fall of more than 1.2 m.

questions.stem: Two deckhands are to scrape a hull from a float alongside, with a drowning hazard. Which set best meets MOHS s. 147?
options: A life jacket each and a verbal promise from the mate to keep an eye on them
Flotation, emergency gear ready, a qualified person standing by, and written procedures
Emergency procedures in the captain's head and a lifebuoy kept in the wheelhouse
A life jacket each, and nothing more is needed for work alongside
questions.explanation: Section 147(1) requires a life jacket (or net or fall-protection system), and s. 147(2) adds readiness of emergency equipment, a qualified person ready to intervene, a vessel in readiness if appropriate, and written emergency procedures.

questions.stem: A crew member sees a spill on a stairway on deck. What does SWPR s. 11 require first?
options: Leave it; only the master needs to know about hazards on deck
Report it at once to the person in charge of the working area
Wait until the end of the shift and mention it at the meeting
Clean it up personally straight away, whatever the substance is
questions.explanation: Section 11(1) requires immediate reporting to the person in charge, and s. 11(2) says correction is done only by a qualified person, with an emergency exception in s. 11(3).

questions.stem: Which of these is something nobody may do under the SWPR?
options: Tamper with a safeguard or safety device
Report a defective tool to the supervisor
Ask for a safety briefing before a new job
Wear gloves while using a hand tool
questions.explanation: Section 9 prohibits tampering with or making ineffective any safeguard or safety device. The other three are acceptable or required.

questions.stem: A worker's ability to work appears impaired by alcohol, in the opinion of the person in charge of the working area. What does s. 14 say?
options: The rule applies only to drugs, not to alcohol
The worker must not be permitted in the working area
The worker may stay if wearing a life jacket at all times
The worker may stay if moved to light duties
questions.explanation: Section 14 says no one may be permitted in a working area whose ability to work is, in the opinion of the person in charge, impaired by alcohol or a drug.

questions.stem: You find that a harness lanyard is frayed. What does MOHS s. 150 expect to happen to it?
options: It is kept in service but used for light work only
It is reported, tagged unsafe and removed from service
It is stowed with the good equipment until the next inspection
It is repaired on the spot with tape and put back
questions.explanation: Section 150(1) requires the employee to report the defect as soon as feasible and s. 150(2) requires the employer to mark or tag it as unsafe and remove it from service.

questions.stem: Which statement about lifting appliances is correct?
options: The safe working load is posted only in the wheelhouse log book
Anyone may operate a lifting appliance under supervision, and a load rating is optional
A load may be left hanging overnight if the area is roped off
A qualified operator, and a safe working load notice fixed to the appliance
questions.explanation: SWPR s. 16 requires a qualified operator, s. 17 requires a permanently affixed safe working load notice, and MOHS s. 213(3) bars leaving a load suspended unless a qualified person is present and in charge.

questions.stem: An opening in the deck leads to a tank 2 m deep. It is not in use and has no coaming. What does SWPR s. 25(1) require?
options: Nothing, because 2 m is too shallow to be a hazard
It need only be marked around the edge with paint
It must be sealed with welded plate before sailing
It must be securely covered or fenced to 900 mm
questions.explanation: Compartments exceeding 1.5 m in depth must be securely covered or fenced to 900 mm unless the opening has a coaming of at least 760 mm. Marking alone is the option only for openings to compartments not exceeding 1.5 m (s. 25(2)).
